title: Archiving and Records Management
overview: Effective records management enables organizations to preserve reliable evidence of their activities, retrieve information quickly, meet operational and accountability requirements, and control the growing volume of physical and electronic information. Poorly organized records can result in lost information, duplication, delayed decisions, unnecessary storage, confidentiality risks, and difficulty demonstrating what occurred and when.

This course provides participants with a practical understanding of the complete records life cycle, from creation and receipt through classification, use, storage, retrieval, retention, archiving, and final disposition. Participants will learn how to distinguish records from general information, establish logical classification and filing structures, apply consistent indexing and naming practices, manage physical and electronic records, and maintain appropriate controls over access and movement.

The program also addresses retention schedules, inactive records, archival transfer, secure disposal, vital records, confidentiality, and the transition toward electronic records management. Practical exercises allow participants to design filing structures, classify sample records, create retrieval controls, and develop improvements for their own records-management environment.
audience: Records officers, document controllers, administrative assistants, executive secretaries, office administrators, coordinators, registry and archive staff, information-management personnel, and employees responsible for creating, receiving, filing, storing, retrieving, protecting, retaining, archiving, or disposing of organizational records.
methodology: The course uses an applied methodology combining facilitator presentations with classification exercises, filing simulations, case studies, records inventories, indexing activities, retention-schedule exercises, physical and electronic records scenarios, group discussions, and practical system-design tasks. Participants will work with realistic records-management situations and develop structures and controls that can be adapted to their own workplace.
objectivesIntro: By the end of the course, participants will be able to:
objectives: Explain the purpose and organizational value of systematic records and archives management.
Distinguish official records from working documents, reference material, and non-record information.
Apply the records life cycle to the creation, use, storage, retention, and disposition of records.
Develop logical classification, filing, indexing, and referencing systems.
Organize physical and electronic records to support accurate and timely retrieval.
Apply appropriate controls for record access, movement, confidentiality, and security.
Use retention schedules to determine how long different records should be maintained.
Manage inactive records, archival transfers, and secure disposition appropriately.
Identify vital records and apply practical protection and continuity measures.
Assess existing records-management practices and identify opportunities for improvement.
